title: The conveyor belt
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Does every client you serve go through the same process?

Jose said to a student who has gone from working for someone to having a business: you are streamlining your product offering so you are not doing things over and over, and explaining different processes to different people. That is too much of a risk.

The final outcome for the client should not vary, he said. Every time you get a client, you put them on that conveyor belt, like the airport. You don't want that bag sitting on the ground somewhere lost, because it isn't on the belt of what you have defined as what you offer.
A student agreed: when there is no process and too many clients, things get lost and people feel forgotten. It is bad branding.

Jose said that he is a little obsessive about process even in his life, and that he gave a detailed list to the people who work at his house. When people leave, you start all over again, so you give the next person the list.

A student said: if you are a leader and a boss and you don't have process, you look unorganized and are not taken as seriously. If you have a process and you say: do this like this, people take you one step more seriously.
Jose said that people get very insecure when they don't understand their job description.

groups.heading: Set the job at the start

lines.text: He described a big company in a business he deals with, whose leader for forty years went to sixteen offices and repeated himself. They had an organization used to leaders who repeated themselves, he said, not a system of accountability. It relies on the charisma of one person.

A student said: you can't teach an old dog new tricks. Jose said: so it is better to get it right off the bat and have job descriptions. If you give a person a new description every day, they resist: you laid out at the beginning what I'd do, and I'm comfortable doing it.
In building a culture, he said, you can teach absorbing new things in the job description. It is about getting the productivity and reaching those goals.
What is your conveyor belt, and which client is off it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the steps every client goes through.
Write who is off the belt right now.
Write each person's job description in three lines.
Write what a new person would need on day one.
Write what changes you will not make to the job once it is set.

check.q: What image did Jose use for process?
choices: A conveyor belt at the airport

check.q: What did a student say about a leader without process?
choices: They look unorganized and are less taken seriously

check.q: What did Jose say is better to do about job descriptions?
choices: Set them right at the start

recap: Put every client on the same belt. Set the job description at the start.
